name: Amy Klobuchar

issue_poll.name: KSTP/SurveyUSA Minnesota Poll #27386, Oct 24–28, 2024 (728 likely voters)
issue_poll.note: Most important issue question; exactly 10 named issues offered (plus Other at 4%). Ranks match the Sept 23–26 KSTP/SurveyUSA poll except order of a few mid items.

issues.position: Pass bills to expand housing supply (Housing Supply and Affordability Act)

votes.question: On the motion to concur in the House amendment with an amendment

issues.note: Final housing package included her regional housing planning grant bill; reintroduced Feb 2024 and cited in her Oct 2024 questionnaire.

issues.position: Codify Roe v. Wade in federal law
issues.note: No floor vote on codifying Roe this term; related VA-rule vote (S.J.Res.103, roll call 72, Yea) not counted.

issues.position: Revive bipartisan border bill; more agents and technology

votes.question: Cloture on the motion to proceed

issues.note: H.R.1 and the FY2026 DHS bill funded Border Patrol agents and technology; she opposed both. The bipartisan bill got no vote.

issues.position: Expand Medicare drug-price negotiation; protect Medicare
issues.note: H.R.1 widened the orphan-drug exemption from Medicare negotiation; her expansion bill got no vote.

issues.position: Apply Social Security tax to earnings above $400,000
issues.note: Stated as part of a debt plan in the Oct 2024 debate; no floor vote on the payroll-tax cap this term.

issues.position: Stronger background checks; ban bump stocks and conversion devices
issues.note: No floor vote on these measures found; Murphy NICS-report amendment (roll call 473, 2025) not counted as it tests none of them.

issues.position: Reduce the debt; no specific spending position found
Require social media firms to report drug trafficking
issues.note: Cooper Davis and Devin Norring Act reintroduced 2025; no floor vote found.

issues.position: Fund police hiring, training, and equipment
issues.note: General funding direction only; no named program or amount.

caveats: Most positions come from her Oct 2024 WCCO/CBS candidate questionnaire and the Oct 2024 debate; her campaign site archive was not reachable.
Immigration rated Contradicted on H.R.1 and the FY2026 DHS appropriations cloture vote, which funded border agents she said she wanted; neither was the bipartisan bill she named.
NFIB said in Aug 2024 she backed making the 20% small-business deduction permanent; not her own statement, so not used (H.R.1, which she opposed, made it permanent).
Economy rated on her named housing-supply bill; the broader 'lower costs' pledge is not testable.
